title: Normalized specialization from endpoint squares
statement: For every finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions], suppose the two restriction fibre squares and the two arbitrary base-change fibre squares hold for all smooth section pairs [def-pur-section-restriction-data], as explicitly stated by [lem-pur-section-fibre-squares]. Then the uniquely coordinate-normalized DNC isomorphism delta [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] intertwines etale restriction on the source and normal pairs, commutes with arbitrary allowed Cartesian base changes, and becomes the identity on the standard rank-zero section after its canonical normal collapse. The endpoint equations are assumptions, not conclusions.

proof.text: Obtain constant-family models kappa and kappa\prime and their one normalization and delta zero-reading formulas. Compare kappa\prime followed by the pullback of restriction with familyRestriction followed by kappa. The given one-fibre square and naturality of the section counit show equality at one. One-fibre detection gives equality on the family. Reading at zero and using the given zero-fibre square, cancel the model isomorphisms to prove the restriction equation for delta. The private normalized_readings_square and ratio_square prove these steps in Lean.

For base change apply constant_family_base_change to the chosen models, the canonical family base comparison, and the canonical source base comparison. The given one-fibre base square and model normalizations supply its one-reading hypothesis. Its zero-reading square, combined with the given zero-fibre base square and the delta zero-reading formulas, yields the claimed equation by ratio_square.

For the standard rank-zero pair obtain the geometric constant model with its two counit readings. One-fibre detection identifies it with the model in the delta formula, since both read as endpointOne. Substitute its zero reading, endpointZero followed by the normal-collapse restriction, and cancel the inverse isomorphisms. This proves RankZero without assuming naturality of delta.
